desc:
For every position i of the integer array nums, find the nearest position j < i to its left whose value is strictly smaller than nums[i]. Return an array answer where answer[i] is that index j, or -1 if no element to the left of i is smaller.

Example: nums = [4, 2, 5, 3, 1, 6] gives [-1, -1, 1, 1, -1, 4]. For the value 3 at index 3, the nearest smaller value on its left is 2 at index 1.
constraints: Equal values do not count as smaller
hints: Checking all earlier positions for every position is O(n<sup>2</sup>). Think about which earlier elements could ever be the answer for some later element.
If an earlier element is larger than or equal to a newer element, the earlier one is never the nearest smaller value for anything to the right of the newer element.
Scan left to right with a stack of indices. Pop while the top value is ≥ nums[i]; the new top (if any) is the answer; then push i.
editorial: Keep a stack of candidate indices whose values strictly increase from bottom to top. When a new element x arrives, every candidate with a value ≥ x is useless from now on: x is closer to the future and not larger, so any later element that could use the old candidate can use x (or something even better) instead. Pop those candidates.

After the pops, the top of the stack (if there is one) is the nearest index on the left with a strictly smaller value. Record it, then push i. Every index is pushed once and popped at most once, so the whole scan is O(n) time and O(n) space. This is the basic monotonic stack pattern that the rest of this topic builds on.
